chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Unissued tapes, retirement and model trains
summary: He may let Jim Rivers issue his tapes, plans a model railway in retirement, and says he cannot believe he is seventy-four.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Okay and then sometime in the future, you've given thought to when maybe you're slowing down playing almost completely as you might start going back through some of your unissued music that you've got - that's always a possibility for the future - isn't it?
Well, you know, I have many tapes--

And, uh, that's why I wanted to work out with Jim Rivers; I think if anyone is going to issue that stuff - I think I should let him do it and, uh, oh - say -"the Best of Wild Bill" - to take a lot of things that maybe people haven't heard and make albums and so on. But, that's something I can do when I retire.
This is something-- my point is that you're playing music and you're looking ahead constantly and this is something extremely worthwhile for somebody of your generation.

Well, I suppose -- I just don't really care to think of myself doing anything else -- of course, I got my retirement mapped out and this year, while I'm in Germany, I'm going to start collecting my engines for my model railway-- I'm going to build one of those and I think I've always been too active and I can do many things with my hands--
As you said the other day, "I can't believe I'm 74 years old".
Well, I certainly don't feel it.
You don't feel it; you don't look it; you don't act it.
But, I'm going to have to be busy as a retired musician; I'm going to have to have something to do and if I can't do anything else but build model railways - that will keep me busy.

Well, the interesting thing about this and maybe we could end the tape with this - is five years ago, when you were 69, you said to me - I'll be satisfied and lucky if I can play two or three more years.
Well, you're still saying that five years from now - so, who knows?
Who knows is right -- and who knows when my teeth are going to fall out.
